explanation.sentence: This patient has new chest pain, insulin-treated diabetes, two-vessel coronary disease involving the left anterior descending and left circumflex arteries, and a reduced ejection fraction.

CABG is the best choice because diabetes and impaired left ventricular function favor surgical revascularization in multivessel disease involving the LAD, particularly when the LAD lesion is proximal.
By contrast, angioplasty with stenting is generally favored for anatomically suitable one- or two-vessel disease when left ventricular function is preserved.
Extended-release nitrates can relieve angina, and heparin may be used acutely if an acute coronary syndrome is suspected, but neither provides definitive revascularization.
